§C.10 Ground Truth — Tables 1-3

What to do, when producing ground truth, in the cases the table rules on detection, boundaries and headers leave to review. Each step serves the rule it links to; the rule decides the output.

Situation Step Rule
A page mixes form fields with a ruled grid Render the grid as a table and the fields as key-value lines, then flag the page Is This Even a Table§9.1.5 · Forms and Key-Value Regions§10.1
A region is a form, a trailing total outside a frame, a data grid under a chart, or detached aligned cells Decide it by that case's own rule, not by the relation test alone Is This Even a Table§9.1.5
A value in a whitespace-aligned block straddles two column tracks Place it in the track its left edge is closest to and flag the page Borderless Whitespace Tables§9.1.1
A printed form grid has no values entered Keep every empty row and flag the page, so a reviewer can see the grid was empty rather than missed Empty Pre-Printed Grids§9.1.3
A form prints dozens of identical empty rows Transcribe them all rather than a few, and flag the page Empty Pre-Printed Grids§9.1.3
A header row cannot be joined to a body (gap, mismatched columns, something in between) Write the header line as text and flag the page; when the gap makes the join doubtful, do not merge Header-Only Tables§9.1.4
A fragment's title carries (cont'd), (continued) or similar Keep the marker and note in the review record that the fragment continues an earlier table Continued in the Title§9.2.3
A table continues across a page break Keep each fragment on its own page as printed, and set the continuation flags on both fragments after looking at both pages Cross-Page Tables§4.3
Column headers are printed again at the foot of a page's block Keep the repeat as a row and flag the page Cross-Page Tables§4.3
A paragraph, caption or heading sits between two fragments sharing one header Merge while the second fragment depends on the header; flag the page when the material in the gap could read as a new section Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9
A row-label column is printed once beside several value blocks Place the blocks as further columns of the labelled table and flag the page so the choice is visible Split Tables Sharing a Header§9.2.9
Stacked header lines could be a wrap or a tier Run the rule / self-standing-leaves / span test deliberately, not by eye Header Wrap vs Real Tier§9.3.2
A header stack is finished Count the leaf tracks and check that every header row adds up to that count before moving on Multi-Row Header Tiers§9.3.3
A units line could go either way Take the second header row and keep that choice for the whole document Units Row§9.3.5 · Choices Made Once Per Document§4.2
A table may be printed twice Decide from the rendered page image, not the text layer Duplicated Tables§9.2.4
